parts.text: Suggest how you would investigate which educational strategy is best for a child who is gifted.

parts.label: (b)

text: Psychological evidence supports many different strategies for educating children with special
needs. I want to know which is best for educating my gifted child.

Psychology and Health
Section A
Answer this question.

text: You have devised a new intelligence test. You test it on some friends but they say that it gives a
very different IQ score from the official test done by the school. One friend complains that the
score she got three weeks ago on your test has now gone down by 20 points.

parts.label: (b)

parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about health promotion.

will do.

text: At the end of a consultation with their medical practitioner, people often say that they will take all
their prescribed medication. But there is a difference between what people say and what they do.

Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have found out about noise.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
“We have control but no ecological validity.” Evaluate what psychologists have found out about
noise and include a debate about the extent to which studies conducted in a laboratory apply
to everyday life. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you could gather data on how people feel when their personal space is invaded.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Give two reasons why invading personal space is unethical.

text: Invading personal space is unethical. We know this because studies have shown that when space
is invaded people will leave a situation earlier than if their space is not invaded. Studies never
investigate how people feel when their space is invaded.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the theory and effects of social overload. 
Psychology and Abnormality
Section A
Answer this question.

text: You have heard that people living in cities behave more negatively compared to those from rural
communities. It is said that this is because people in a city suffer from ‘social overload’ whereas
those in rural communities do not.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:

parts.text: Describe the main features of electro-convulsive therapy.

parts.label: (b)

text: After electro-convulsive therapy (ECT) many patients report memory loss. However, the evidence
for this is not conclusive.

Section A
Answer this question.

text: Some people have obsessions, some have compulsions and some have both obsessions and
compulsions. As a Clinical Psychologist diagnosing a new patient you will need to decide which of
these the patient has before choosing the treatment.

Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest a strategy to find out whether followers really have accepted a leadership decision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the Vroom and Yetton normative decision theory.

text: The Vroom and Yetton normative decision theory includes what is known as decision acceptance
which is the degree to which a follower accepts a decision made by a leader.
